title: Randomized time is contained in bounded-error time
statement: For every function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RTIME}(T) \subseteq \mathrm{BPTIME}(T)$. Both classes allow a finite randomized machine running in time bounded by a constant multiple of $T$; in $\mathrm{RTIME}(T)$ it halts on every branch, accepts members with probability at least $2/3$, and never accepts nonmembers, while in $\mathrm{BPTIME}(T)$ it outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least $2/3$ on every input.
